explanation: WCAG 2.2 introduced SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) at Level AA, requiring targets to be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where spacing perimeter, inline text, user agent defaults, or essential presentations apply. (In contrast, SC 2.5.5 Target Size at Level AAA requires 44 by 44 CSS pixels).

distractorNotes.b: 44 by 44 CSS pixels is the enhanced Level AAA threshold in SC 2.5.5, not the Level AA minimum in SC 2.5.8.
distractorNotes.c: WCAG specifications measure target sizes in CSS pixels, not variable physical hardware device pixels.
distractorNotes.d: 12 by 12 CSS pixels is too small and fails both Level AA and Level AAA target size requirements.

sourceNote: W3C Understanding SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) establishes 24x24 CSS pixels minimum at Level AA.

stem: In the Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines (ATAG) 2.0, how is the scope divided between Part A and Part B?

options.text: Part A governs native desktop editing software applications, while Part B governs web-based content management platforms.
Part A ensures the authoring tool UI is accessible, while Part B ensures the tool supports generating accessible web content.
Part A establishes normative technical conformance criteria, while Part B specifies non-normative advisory techniques.
Part A covers automated accessibility evaluation engines, while Part B governs manual rich text authoring environments.

explanation: ATAG 2.0 is structured into two main parts: Part A focuses on making the authoring tool user interface itself accessible to authors with disabilities (following WCAG principles for software). Part B focuses on supporting the authoring tool's ability to produce accessible web content (enabling, preserving, and checking accessibility).

distractorNotes.a: ATAG 2.0 applies across both desktop and web-based authoring software; its division into parts is based on tool UI accessibility versus output accessibility, not software platform.
distractorNotes.c: Both Part A and Part B contain normative success criteria as well as non-normative techniques; the division separates tool UI accessibility from content production support.
distractorNotes.d: Automated evaluation features and manual authoring interfaces are both covered under Part B (guidelines B.2, B.3, and B.4) rather than split across parts.

sourceNote: W3C ATAG 2.0 §Structure defines Part A (accessible tool UI) and Part B (supporting accessible content generation).

stem: Under ATAG 2.0 Guideline B.2, what requirement must an authoring tool satisfy when converting content between formats?

options.text: It must require the author to manually re-enter all alternative text and structural metadata after conversion.
It must translate non-standard markup elements into proprietary tool-specific metadata tags.
It must preserve accessibility information (such as alt text and heading structure) during content transformations.
It must generate an external conformance claim document certifying the target format conforms to WCAG.

explanation: ATAG 2.0 Guideline B.2 requires authoring tools to preserve accessibility information during content transformations, conversions, and migrations. For example, when converting a document from a word processing format to HTML or PDF, alternative text, headings, table structures, and language tags must be retained.

distractorNotes.a: ATAG B.2 mandates automated preservation of existing accessibility information during conversion.
distractorNotes.b: Authoring tools must output standard accessible web content rather than proprietary markup formats.
distractorNotes.d: Guideline B.2 focuses on preserving document accessibility data, not generating conformance claim files.

sourceNote: W3C ATAG 2.0 Guideline B.2 mandates preserving accessibility information during content transformations.

stem: In the European standard EN 301 549, how are the accessibility requirements for web content in Chapter 9 determined?

options.text: By defining a separate set of proprietary European Union accessibility rules distinct from W3C standards.
By referencing United States Section 508 standards without incorporating any international criteria.
By mandating that all web content must satisfy WCAG 2.1 Level AAA success criteria without exceptions.
By directly adopting and harmonizing with the W3C WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA success criteria.

explanation: Chapter 9 of EN 301 549 ('Web') directly harmonizes with and adopts W3C WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA success criteria as its technical accessibility requirements for web pages and web applications across European public and private procurement.

distractorNotes.a: EN 301 549 explicitly harmonizes with W3C WCAG rather than creating competing proprietary European rules.
distractorNotes.b: EN 301 549 is a European EN standard harmonized with W3C WCAG, not a copy of US Section 508.
distractorNotes.c: EN 301 549 requires Level A and Level AA conformance; Level AAA is not legally mandated.

sourceNote: ETSI EN 301 549 Chapter 9 adopts W3C WCAG 2.1 Level AA as normative requirements for web content.
